"""Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation. Responsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block starts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to `mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes. Each block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start rule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never names a concrete type. """ from __future__ import annotations from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable from dataclasses import dataclass from mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions TAB_STOP = 4 SPACE_CHARS = " \t" # A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after # advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched. StartRule = Callable[["Cursor", "Block"], "Block | None"] # A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only # when it returns True. ContinueRule = Callable[["Block", "Cursor"], bool] # An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines. AddLineRule = Callable[["Block", "Cursor"], None] # A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content. FinalizeRule = Callable[["Block"], None] def next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int: """Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.""" if char == "\t": return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP return col + 1 def indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int: """Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.""" end = pos end_col = col while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS: end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col) end += 1 return end_col - col class Cursor: """A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.""" def __init__(self, line: str) -> None: self.line = line self.pos = 0 self.col = 0 @property def rest(self) -> str: """The text from the current position to the end of the line.""" return self.line[self.pos :] @property def indent(self) -> int: """Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.""" return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col) def next_nonspace(self) -> int: """Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.""" end = self.pos while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS: end += 1 return end def is_blank(self) -> bool: """True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.""" return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line) def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None: """Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.""" while self.pos < index: self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) self.pos += 1 def advance_nonspace(self) -> None: """Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.""" self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace()) def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None: """Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed. A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot. """ target = self.col + columns while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS: self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) self.pos += 1 class Block: """A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.""" def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None: self.kind = kind self.parent: Block | None = None self.children: list[Block] = [] self.is_open = True self.lines: list[str] = [] self.content = "" # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one. self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None: """The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.""" if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open: return self.children[-1] return None @dataclass(frozen=True) class BlockType: """The rules that define one kind of block. `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks. """ name: str continues: ContinueRule is_container: bool = False accepts_lines: bool = False interruptible: bool = False lazy: bool = False start: StartRule | None = None add_line: AddLineRule | None = None finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None def __post_init__(self) -> None: if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None: raise ValueError(f"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule") if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines: raise ValueError(f"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines") def _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool: return True def _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool: return not cursor.is_blank() def _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None: cursor.advance_nonspace() block.lines.append(cursor.rest) def _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None: """Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text. A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree. """ text = "\n".join(block.lines).strip(" \t") block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block)) if not block.content and block.parent is not None: block.parent.children.remove(block) def _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap: """The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.""" root = block while root.parent is not None: root = root.parent assert root.references is not None return root.references DOCUMENT = BlockType("document", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True) PARAGRAPH = BlockType( "paragraph", continues=_paragraph_continues, accepts_lines=True, interruptible=True, lazy=True, add_line=_paragraph_add_line, finalize=_paragraph_finalize, ) class BlockRegistry: """The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules. Start rules are tried in registration order. The fallback type is the paragraph created when no start rule matches a line of text. """ def __init__(self, root: BlockType, fallback: BlockType) -> None: self.root = root self.fallback = fallback self._names: set[str] = set() self._starts: list[BlockType] = [] self.register(root) self.register(fallback) def register(self, block_type: BlockType) -> None: """Add a block type. Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order.""" if block_type.name in self._names: raise ValueError(f"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}") self._names.add(block_type.name) if block_type.start is not None: self._starts.append(block_type) def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]: """The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order.""" return tuple(self._starts) DEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH) class DocumentParser: """Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time.""" def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None: self.registry = registry self.root = Block(registry.root) self.root.references = ReferenceMap() def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None: """Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text.""" cursor = Cursor(line) # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation. container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor) all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds. started = False while not self._is_text_leaf(container): new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container) if new_block is None: break if not started: started = True all_closed = True self._close_below(container) self._attach(new_block, container) container = new_block # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block. tip = self._tip() if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy: self._add_line(tip, cursor) return self._close_below(container) if container.kind.accepts_lines: self._add_line(container, cursor) elif not cursor.is_blank(): paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback) self._attach(paragraph, container) self._add_line(paragraph, cursor) def finish(self) -> Block: """Close every open block and return the document root.""" self._close_below(self.root) self.root.is_open = False return self.root def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block: container = self.root while True: child = container.open_last_child() if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor): return container container = child def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None: for block_type in self.registry.starts(): assert block_type.start is not None new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container) if new_block is not None: return new_block return None def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool: return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None: """Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it.""" while not container.kind.is_container: self._finalize(container) assert container.parent is not None container = container.parent container.children.append(new_block) new_block.parent = container def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None: assert block.kind.add_line is not None block.kind.add_line(block, cursor) def _tip(self) -> Block: """The deepest open block.""" tip = self.root while (child := tip.open_last_child()) is not None: tip = child return tip def _close_below(self, container: Block) -> None: child = container.open_last_child() if child is None: return self._close_below(child) self._finalize(child) def _finalize(self, block: Block) -> None: block.is_open = False if block.kind.finalize is not None: block.kind.finalize(block) def parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> Block: """Build the block tree for `lines`, which hold no line-ending characters.""" parser = DocumentParser(registry) for line in lines: parser.incorporate_line(line) return parser.finish() ---- """HTML rendering.
